Authors: Azimi M.; Soltani A.; Mirzababaei M.; Jaksa M.B.; Ashwath N.
Title: Biopolymer stabilization of clayey soil

Soil_Name: Kaolin-bentonite blend (KB) artificial clayey soil, 75% kaolin : 25% bentonite dry mass

Form: Granular powder dissolved in distilled water (aqueous biopolymer solution used as mixing/compaction liquid)

Curing_Condition: Sealed (multiple layers of cling wrap to prevent moisture loss), ambient laboratory temperature
Value_Source: derived: UCS_treated = q0 x (1 + IMP/100) = 302.3 x (1 + 8/100); IMP read from Fig. 3d data label (graph-estimated IMP, exact UCS computed arithmetically)
Page_Table_Figure: Table 2 (soil); Table 3 (CS); Table 5 (mix design); Fig. 3d; Section 4, p.2808
Notes: Dosage definition: DBP is the SOLID BIOPOLYMER-TO-WATER MASS RATIO, DBP = M_BP/M_W x 100 (Eq. 1), NOT % of dry soil. The biopolymer solution-to-dry-soil ratio is fixed at the target OMC of 22%, so the equivalent biopolymer-to-dry-soil mass ratio = DBP x 0.22 = 0.055% (paper's stated conversion; e.g. 1% solution at 20% OMC -> ~0.2% of dry soil). Chitosan_Content_% column holds biopolymer-to-DRY-SOIL % (converted = DBP x 0.22 for cross-study comparability); original DBP (biopolymer-to-water %) = 0.25%. 7-d IMP = 8%, 28-d IMP = 29% relative to unamended q0 = 302.3 kPa (Fig. 3d data labels). LL/PL/PI of treated soil NOT measured. 1.5% CS = optimum dosage; CS ranked most effective of the four biopolymers (28 d IMP 104%). Rate of UCS reduction beyond optimum: R7 = 415.8 kPa/%, R28 = 521.0 kPa/% (highest of all biopolymers).
